report.scope: Synthetic relevance judgments and regression signals, not user satisfaction, provider throughput or a real-library audit.

method.relevance: NDCG uses graded gains 2^grade-1 and unique canonical eligible candidates; incomplete judgments produce null.
method.precision: Grade >= 2 among judged returned slots; fill is measured separately. Missing judgments are never negative votes.
method.freshness: Publication age only, <=30 days; unknown dates are excluded from the denominator and counted separately.
method.diversity: Maximum share by source+creator; the limit is inapplicable with fewer than two relevant creators.
method.exposure: Previous synthetic shelf overlap is distinct from viewing history; no production exposure ledger is created.

cases.intent: Liked racing evidence should outrank cooking; an explicitly rejected title is forbidden.
A prolific liked creator must share the shelf with other relevant creators.
Mechanical source/format/creator tags are not positive topic evidence.
With equally relevant topics, prefer known recent publications; unknown dates remain unmeasured.
Repeated shelf exposure is separate from watched history and should be visible as a diagnostic gap.
Observed racing preferences should guide VOD picks while a one-star broadcast is excluded.
Measure avoidable creator concentration separately from relevance.
New ingestion is not proof of a new publication; freshness must report known/unknown separately.
